transcript:
Meeting Header: Recorded at 2026-10-21T15:00:00-07:00, Duration: ~45 minutes. Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Evelyn Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (Birchwood Head of InfoSec), Tom Reynolds (Birchwood Platform), Priya Malhotra (Birchwood Compliance), Daniel Wu (Birchwood DevOps).

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC security sync. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the open items from last week.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Hi all, Aisha here. We're mostly focused on SSO, logs, and retention this week.
[00:18] Tom Reynolds: Tom here, same — will share some log samples.
[00:22] Marcus Chen: Marcus from Redwood, I'll run the bench and answer infra questions.
[00:27] [00:30] Lena Park: Great. Quick recap: we promised SOC2 artifacts and pen test summary, an SSO metadata step-by-step, and Marcus to run a dedicated benchmark for our hosted vs dedicated config. Action items? We'll confirm.
[01:05] Aisha Khan: For SSO, our IdP is Okta, SAML 2.0. We need SP-initiated flow, auto-provisioning optional. Also need SCIM for groups later.
[01:23] Marcus Chen: Okta is common, we support SAML SSO and SCIM. For the POC we usually do SAML first, then SCIM in a follow-up. Note: some of our docs show the metadata XML with entity redirect URLs, sometimes the hostnames get munged in the export — sorry the auto-export can show 'redwood-infrerence' once in a while, small transcribe error in doc.
[01:48] Tom Reynolds: Ha, I saw that 'infrerence' typo earlier. No problem as long as keys line up. Also curious — do you support signed assertions only, or do you do encrypted assertions?
[02:04] Marcus Chen: We require signed assertions; encrypted assertions are supported but it's not default. If you want encrypted assertions we can enable and test it in the dedicated/staging environment.
[02:21] [02:30] Priya Malhotra: For compliance, we need audit trails that show who accessed what data, and we need to ensure logs are immutable for at least 7 years for some products — can you support long-term retention or an export path?
[02:46] Marcus Chen: Redwood keeps audit logs centrally and you can configure retention per-customer on Dedicated. For hosted customers we have default retention of 90 days but we provide log export APIs and S3 export so you can ship to your archive. The export format is newline-delimited JSON with event types; we'll share a sample.
[03:11] Aisha Khan: Sample would be great. Also, are audit logs tamper-evident? We need a chain-of-custody for some regulators.
[03:24] Marcus Chen: We provide append-only storage with write-once policies on Dedicated and audit signing for exported bundles. I should note, in the hosted product we rely on cloud provider storage with signed log feeds; for Dedicated we can provide stronger hermetic guarantees.
[03:45] [04:00] Lena Park: Action — Marcus will send sample logs and a doc describing the tamper-evidence features.
[04:12] Daniel Wu: How about access control — RBAC model? We need fine-grained roles: admin, auditor, engine-ops, app-integration. Can those map to SAML groups?
[04:31] Marcus Chen: Yes, you can map SAML groups via SCIM or via attribute mappings. We expose roles and you can bind them to SAML group names. We'll include a template mapping in the SSO guide.
[04:49] [05:00] Tom Reynolds: KMS — our bank policy requires customer-managed keys for production. Do you support BYOK and HSM imports?
[05:12] Marcus Chen: We support both: bring-your-own-key (KMS integration) for Hosted (via key wrapping with a CloudKMS provider) and full HSM integration for Private/Dedicated. For strict key custody we recommend Private deployment with HSM and VPC peering.
[05:35] Aisha Khan: For POC, will plain BYOK suffice or do we need Dedicated right away?
[05:44] Marcus Chen: For functional testing BYOK in hosted is fine. For formal audits where auditors need to see key custody controls, Dedicated or Private with HSM is the recommended path. We can show the control mappings against SOC2.
[06:05] [06:30] Priya Malhotra: On SOC2, can you share the Type II report and any recent pentest? That'll speed our internal risk review.
[06:40] Lena Park: Yes — we have the SOC2 Type II report and a recent penetration test summary. I'll upload both to the secure share after the call.
[06:49] Marcus Chen: Also note some pen test items were around model-scoring endpoints and rate limiting; we've got mitigations in our runtime — continuous batching and quota enforcement — I might've mis-said 'continuous blaching' in a doc earlier, transcription flub.
[07:10] [07:30] Tom Reynolds: Good to hear mitigations exist. Can you produce an attestation mapping to our internal control framework?
[07:40] Lena Park: We can provide a mapping matrix of Redwood controls to your control IDs. That often helps the risk team.
[07:49] Aisha Khan: Great. Regarding data residency, some of our customers must stay in-region. Your hosted offering lists EU/NA regions — can you guarantee region pinning for the POC?
[08:05] Marcus Chen: Yes, for the POC we can pin region to us-west or eu-west depending on the data. For production, Dedicated gives explicit region isolation. For very strict residency we also have Private on-prem options.
[08:24] [08:45] Daniel Wu: If we do benchmarking, will the results differ much between hosted and dedicated? We're worried about tail latency under load.
[08:56] Marcus Chen: Dedicated removes noisy neighbors and gives predictable throughput; hosted is more variable but often fine for most workloads. We'll run a benchmark that includes 99th percentile tail latency and a token-cost analysis.
[09:18] Tom Reynolds: Also curious about KV cache persistence across restarts — if we use a long-running session, does your runtime persist cache or is it ephemeral?
[09:31] Marcus Chen: KV cache is ephemeral per runtime instance; we have warm-starting and prefix caching at the routing layer but we don't persist user-level KV cache across sessions for privacy reasons. If you need deterministic reuse you can use our recommended cache key strategy.
[09:52] [10:00] Priya Malhotra: On retention — we need record-level deletion for GDPR right-to-be-forgotten. Can you delete all log traces and model inputs for a given user?
[10:12] Marcus Chen: We support per-customer retention policies and deletion requests. For hosted, deletion is queued and we provide confirmation. For Dedicated/Private you have direct control and can run deletion scripts. Note that backups have retention timelines; we'll include the backup deletion window in the doc.
[10:40] [11:00] Lena Park: Let's go over the shared artifacts: I've uploaded a security-deck link in the calendar notes and will add SOC2 + pen test to the secure share.
[11:17] Aisha Khan: Where's the secure share? We need an S3 presigned or a vendor portal.
[11:23] Lena Park: We'll use a presigned S3 link; I'll send via our encrypted email.
[11:28] [12:00] Tom Reynolds: One minor ask — can we get a sanitized sample of model input/output to show to risk? We just need structure, not customer data.
[12:12] Marcus Chen: Yes, we can generate sanitized examples and include them in the benchmark pack.
[12:24] [13:00] Priya Malhotra: Any known gaps vs SOC2 controls? We're mostly concerned about change management and incident response.
[13:14] Marcus Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and our incident response and change mgmt are part of the report. There was an earlier item around third-party dependency tracking; we've since improved SBOM and vendor attestations. I'll point to that section in the report.
[13:40] [14:00] Lena Park: Quick timeline check — our goal is to complete the POC bench and security artifacts by end of month. Does that still work for Birchwood?
[14:11] Aisha Khan: Yes, end of month is OK; deliverables: SOC2+pen test by 10/23, benchmark week of 10/26, log samples and retention doc by 10/25.
[14:25] Daniel Wu: I'll coordinate for the bench and provide test accounts.
[14:33] [15:00] Marcus Chen: I'll schedule the bench and share the test plan (qps, model configs, sequence lengths) to make it reproducible. NOTE: we'll measure p50/p95/p99 and token-cost.
[15:15] Tom Reynolds: For the bench, include TLS mutual auth test if possible, we want to test mTLS for private endpoints.
[15:26] Marcus Chen: Yes, we'll include an mTLS variant on the dedicated cluster.
[15:33] [16:00] Priya Malhotra: On audit logs again — do you support streaming to our SIEM (Splunk/QRadar)?
[16:12] Marcus Chen: Yes, we support log shipping via Kinesis / PubSub / direct S3 export; we can provide a connector example for Splunk HTTP Event Collector.
[16:28] Aisha Khan: Perfect. Any outstanding legal/procurement items?
[16:34] Lena Park: We exchanged an NDA earlier; procurement will likely want standard MSA and DPA. Our legal is ready to review once you indicate intent to proceed to Dedicated.
[16:46] [17:00] Daniel Wu: One more question — data encryption at rest: algorithm details? AES-256?
[17:06] Marcus Chen: We use AES-256-GCM for at-rest encryption and TLS 1.3 for in-flight. For BYOK and HSM we can provide FIPS-validated modules.
[17:18] [18:00] Lena Park: Let's summarize next steps out loud: Lena to send SOC2 and pen test by 10/23; Marcus to schedule benchmarks for week of 10/26 and provide SSO guide + sample logs by 10/25; Tom to share retention policy by 10/25; Priya to finalize control list by 10/28.
[18:40] Aisha Khan: That matches our expectations. Thanks.
[18:46] Lena Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and the secure share link.
[18:55] [19:00] Meeting ended.

Notes: Transcript has some auto-transcription artifacts (typos like 'infrerence', occasional name swapping). Shared artifacts: security-deck.pdf (calendar), SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (secure share after call), pen_test_summary_2026.pdf (secure share), sample-logs-ndjson.zip (to be attached), sso-saml-guide.md (to be attached).
